newsitem.title: SPAIN: Retevision sale offer fails to impress BCH bidder.
newsitem.headline: Retevision sale offer fails to impress BCH bidder.

text.p: Privatisation conditions for a 60 percent stake in Spain's second basic telephone operator Retevision are not particularly good, according to the one group which has concretely expressed an interest in the bidding.
"The (sale) conditions are not very favourable and it's not clear if we will participate in the bidding," a spokesman for the BCH consortium told Reuters.
The consortium, comprised of Banco Central Hispano, France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom, had expressed interest in Retevision but was awaiting the terms of the share sale.
The Retevision stake is due to be sold by mid-year. The firm will have the ambitious task of competing with the recently-privatised domestic operator Telefonica.
Last week, Retevision's board approved the conditions for the sale of a 60 percent stake in the firm for a minimum price of 45.6 billion pesetas.
The bidder will be obliged to underwrite a 10 percent capital increase in the firm, with a further payment of 25.33 billion pesetas.
The spokesman for the BCH consortium said its main bugbear was the connection charges which Retevision will have to pay Telefonica for using its network, recently approved by the government.
The tariffs announced "are not so good that they assure the viability of the project from the start," the spokesman said.
The government approved an average tariff of 5.1 pesetas per minute to be paid by Retevision for using Telefonica's services.

"We have yet to study the connection tariffs and, at the same time, conversations with other groups interested in buying Retevision are still going on, so it seems we'll use up the time limit to April 21 to decide whether or not to request participation (in the bidding)," he said.

Underwriting a 10 percent capital increase was not a disadvantage in the sale conditions, he added, as this would mean that the buyer would have more power over minority shareholders, having a stake of more than two-thirds of capital.

Apart from the BCH consortium, Endesa has said it is likely to be involved in the Retevision auction and press reports today linked the electricity firm with the Italian operator Stet to present a second offer.
The period for presentation of bids ends on June 9, and the auction will be resolved in 60 days.
Retevision hopes to provide an alternative to Telefonica's services in Spain before the end of the year.
